name: Muldoons channel walls
summary: Gunditjmara builders added multi-tiered basalt walls along the older Muldoons channel at Lake Condah about 1150 to 1350 CE, part of a stone fish-trap system.
description: Multi-tiered basalt walls added along the pre-existing F10 channel.
tier_reason: A wall-phase demotion may be sensible, but its construction/phasing source is still unread; preserve that qualification rather than agreeing to an authenticated identity. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.label: by c. 1350 CE (inferred)
date.basis: The authors date construction and initial use of the later walled F10 channel approximately c. 1150–1350 CE (600–800 cal BP), based on sediment mixing.

events.statement: Archaeological interpretation places initial use of F10 with its later walls within c. 1150–1350 CE.
applications: water management within the F10 fishery complex
events.population: Gunditjmara users of the Muldoons F10 water channel
events.caveats: This approximate archaeological interpretation is not a hard upper bound, a directly witnessed catch or proof of uninterrupted use since the older channel. The source was inspected online; no local copy could be retained in the current pass.

evidence.supports: The authors distinguish earlier F10 excavation from later walls, and infer construction and initial use of the walled channel around 600–800 cal BP.

date.label: c. 1150–1350
date.basis: Article assigns walls to c. 600–800 cal BP; conversion uses BP=1950.

events.statement: Multi-tiered basalt walls added along the pre-existing F10 channel.
events.caveats: A long sedimentary hiatus separates phases; continuous operation or unchanged knowledge transmission is not established.

evidence.supports: Later rock-wall construction and its relationship to the excavated channel.

earliest_record.rationale: Historian/date dispute retained. A later community witness is not an automatic earliest-record anchor.

community_entry.community: Gunditjmara users of the Muldoons F10 water channel
community_entry.rationale: Archaeological interpretation places initial use of F10 with its later walls within c. 1150–1350 CE.
community_entry.proxy_reason: Use is an archaeological interpretation of the later constructed water-channel context; it does not convert the much older infill date into an observed fishing-use date.
community_entry.caveats: This approximate archaeological interpretation is not a hard upper bound, a directly witnessed catch or proof of uninterrupted use since the older channel. The source was inspected online; no local copy could be retained in the current pass.

caveats: A long sedimentary hiatus separates phases; continuous operation or unchanged knowledge transmission is not established.

links.statement: Later basalt walls modified the sides of the previously excavated F10 channel.
links.scope: Muldoons Trap Complex, Gunditjmara Country; modification c. 1150–1350 CE.
links.alternatives: Other trap features and maintenance strategies are not assigned this chronology.
links.caveats: No claim of continuous use, unbroken transmission or regional simultaneity.
links.timing: The early node dates basal infill evidence; the later dated modification follows a sedimentary hiatus.

evidence.supports: Authors distinguish initial block removal and later added rock walls in the same feature.
